narrative:
The model determined that you have a 25% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

Your denial was driven primarily by three aspects of your financial profile. The most influential factor was your savings account status. Having no savings or an unknown balance is relatively common among applicants, yet in your case it pushed the prediction toward higher risk. The second most important factor was your property ownership. Although you own real estate, which is generally viewed positively, this feature still contributed somewhat toward viewing you as higher risk compared with approved applicants. Finally, your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income also mattered. Your rate of 1% is notably lower than the average of about 3% among those who were approved, and this lower burden actually worked in your favor by pulling the prediction slightly toward good credit.

Taken together, the absence of savings and your property situation outweighed the positive effect of your low monthly repayment burden, tipping the overall assessment into the denial range.

You should focus on building verifiable savings and perhaps waiting until you have a longer, stable employment record before reapplying. These steps typically improve how lenders view applications like yours. (218 words)
